title: Mitigate retry amplification and connection pool leak causing elevated 5xxs for Hosted API
creator: Ariella Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers escalated recurring 5xx/timeouts and elevated latency when their clients retried requests. Investigation shows a repeatable pattern: transient upstream 502/504 triggers client retries -> simultaneous retries amplify traffic -> our HTTP connection pool and proxy logic hit a leak/queueing degredation path for streaming requests which then returns 5xx or times out. This ticket tracks the engineering fixes (server-side and gateway-level), the rollout plan, observability additions, and customer comms.
acceptance_criteria: Observed 75% reduction in retry-originated 5xxs for affected routes in canary cluster after rollout
No new connection_fd leaks reported in staging under heavy retry-simulation (stress harness)
New retry and connection metrics are visible in Grafana and alerting triggers for >5% retry amplification on any route
SDK hosted default retry policy updated and documented; enterprise customers can opt-in to legacy behavior via tenant flag
investigation_notes: 2026-03-08: On-call alerted by Customer Success: periodic bursts of 5xx from customer 'FinLedger' correlated with heavy client-side retries.
Collected pcap+proxy logs: saw spikes in SYN_RECV and TIME_WAIT on proxy pods just prior to 502 spikes.
Heap/FD snapshot on gateway showed retention of idle HTTP/1.1 connections beyond configured keepalive in path that handles streaming responses—suspected stale connection eviction bug.

Reproduced locally with synthetic harness that issues jittered retry storms; replication shows our proxy enters a slow path where requests are queued and connection allocator fails to recycle sockets -> 502/504 from upstream when queue overflows.

Found two contributing code issues: (A) connection pool eviction condition fails when stream flag is set (edge-case for streaming endpoints), (B) retry coordination logic duplicates retries when proxy-level timeout and client retry window overlap (no idempotency collapse).
Risk assessment: high for customers issuing synchronous blocking calls with default SDK retry settings. Also impacts Dedicated clusters with similar proxy code.
fixes: Patch A (hotfix): fix connection pool eviction condition to correctly release idle streaming sockets (PR #14678). This prevents gradual FD leakage under retry storms.
Patch B: add server-side idempotency key handler and request de-duplication gate on the frontend for non-mutating generation endpoints. Collapses simultaneous matching retries within 250ms window.
Patch C: introduce a proxy-level backpressure/circuit-breaker for per-pod in-flight requests that short-circuits and returns 429 with Retry-After rather than cascading timeouts.
Patch D: update default hosted gateway retry policy to jittered exponential backoff (base=150ms, cap=2s, max_retries=3) and add header telemetry for tenant-sdk-version to track clients.
Patch E: add a tenant-level runtime toggle to opt-out of aggressive deduplication for customers relying on exact request semantics.
Perf trade-offs: de-duplication increases memory for short-lived request cache; circuit-breaker may cause 429s for bursty legitimate traffic but reduces 5xx/TTO overall.

deploy_plan: Step 1: Merge hotfix PRs and build canary images (runtime/gateway/sdk)
Step 2: Deploy to staging and run stress harness job 'retry-storm-sim' for 2 hours. Verify no FD growth and <1% 5xx under synthetic retries.
Step 3: Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic for 4 hours. Monitor retry amplification metric and SLOs.
Step 4: Expand to 25% for 6 hours, collect customer-specific telemetry for top-3 impacted tenants.
Step 5: Full rollout with gradual ramp over 12 hours if metrics are stable. Abort/rollback if 5xx rate increases by >10% or error budget burn >15% in any region.
Rollback plan: redeploy previous gateway/runtime images, disable dedupe via tenant toggle, and instruct SDK teams to revert retry changes via config flag.
testing: Unit tests for eviction condition and dedupe cache behavior (added in PRs)
Integration tests: end-to-end requests with streaming payloads and simulated upstream 502s; assert dedupe semantics and no FD leak
Staging chaos run: restart gateway pods under load while running retry-storm-sim to validate resilience
Performance test: measure memory and CPU overhead of dedupe cache at 99th percentile QPS for top-10 customers
Compatibility: run SDK integration test matrix (node/python/go) to ensure header telemetry and retry defaults are backward compatible
monitoring_and_alerting: New alert: RETRY_AMPLIFICATION>0.05 for 5m on any route (severity P1)
New alert: GATEWAY_FD_LEAK rate > 10 incidents per 10m (severity P0)
